page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-192-standardlssd is an x86_64 virtual machine configuration designed for storage-intensive and high-memory cloud computing workloads. The server provisions 192 dedicated vCPUs backed by 1,512 GB of system memory, establishing a memory density of 7.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is not present on this machine type, as it contains zero GPUs.

The primary differentiator of this instance is its direct-attached storage capacity, supplying 45,097 GB of local NVMe SSD storage partitioned across 12 physical drives. This architecture delivers high-throughput, low-latency disk operations directly attached to the host, circumventing network storage layer latency. Networking resources do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating private networking or allocated address pools for external routing.

With its vast local NVMe volume and 1.5 TB memory pool, this server type delivers balanced resource density for input/output bound infrastructure. It is configured primarily for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehouses, large-scale caching systems, and high-volume ETL processing pipelines requiring substantial temporary local scratch capacity.
